The build now passes (exit 0).

**Cause:** the working tree contains a dependency bump from Next 16.2.10 → 16.3.0, which added a required `bfcacheId: string` to `AppRouterInstance`. Sixteen hand-rolled router mocks across nine spec files construct that object as an inline literal, so each one became a type error. They didn't show up in `npm run lint` or the component tests — only `tsc`, which `next build` runs.

**Fix:** added `bfcacheId: ''` to all 16 mock literals, plus the shared `defaultRouter` in [navigation.ts](src/tests/__mocks__/next/navigation.ts) so the module mock stays faithful to the real interface.

Also ran `npm run format`, which fixed `package.json` — `npm-check-updates` had stripped its trailing newline when it wrote the upgrades. That's the format:check warning I flagged earlier; it reformatted the whole file to Prettier's style, hence the 63-line diff, but the dependency versions are untouched.

Checklist, all clean:

- `npm run typecheck` — 0 errors (was 16)
- `npm run lint` — clean
- `npm run format:check` — clean
- `npx knip` — clean
- `npm run test:components` — 697/697 across 80 files
- `op run --env-file ./.env -- npm run build` — exit 0

The three `@mixin` CSS parsing warnings from Turbopack are unrelated and pre-existing — Mantine's PostCSS mixins in `NavBarLinksGroup.module.css` and `UserButton.module.css`. They're warnings only and don't fail the build, so I've left them; say the word if you want me to look at the postcss config.

One thing worth deciding separately: those 16 router mocks are near-identical 7-field literals, so the next Next.js release that touches `AppRouterInstance` will break the build in exactly the same way. A single `makeRouterMock(overrides)` helper in [common.tsx](src/tests/components/lib/common.tsx) would reduce that to one edit. I didn't do it since it's beyond fixing the build — happy to if you want.

**Prettier: no.** It only reformats what's already there — it will re-wrap a long import statement but never rewrite the specifier. (It doesn't even sort imports here; `eslint-plugin-simple-import-sort` does that.)

**ESLint: yes**, two viable routes:

1. **`no-restricted-imports` with `patterns`** — built-in, no new dependency, and lets you attach a custom message pointing at the rule in CLAUDE.md.
2. **`import-x/no-relative-parent-imports`** — `eslint-plugin-import-x` is already installed and configured with the TS resolver. Purpose-built, but the message is generic and it's harder to scope exceptions.

I'd use the first:

```js
'no-restricted-imports': ['error', {
    patterns: [{
        group: ['../*'],
        message: "Use the '@/' alias instead of a parent-relative import (CLAUDE.md § Imports). Same-directory './' imports are fine.",
    }],
}],
```

Neither is auto-fixable, so `--fix` won't rewrite specifiers for you — it flags, you edit.

The catch is what's already in the tree. 64 parent-relative imports in `src/` and `e2e/`, and they split cleanly into two very different groups:

**4 genuine violations**, exactly what the rule is meant to catch:

- [NavBarNested.tsx:8](src/components/NavBarNested/NavBarNested.tsx#L8) → `../NavBarLinksGroup/NavBarLinksGroup`
- [GameDayList.tsx:6](src/components/GameDayList/GameDayList.tsx#L6) → `../GameDayIndicator/GameDayIndicator`
- [GameDayIndicator.tsx:6](src/components/GameDayIndicator/GameDayIndicator.tsx#L6) → `../GameDayLink/GameDayLink`
- [mdx-components.vitest.spec.tsx:9](src/docs/mdx-components.vitest.spec.tsx#L9) → `../../mdx-components`

The first three become `@/components/…` trivially. The fourth can't — `mdx-components.tsx` sits at the repo root and `@/*` only maps to `./src/*`, so it needs either an exemption or a new tsconfig path.

**60 in `__mocks__/` directories**, all one uniform pattern — a mock importing the thing it mocks one level up:

```ts
// src/components/FamilyTree/__mocks__/FamilyTree.tsx
import { Props } from '../FamilyTree';
```

These are arguably the spirit of the permitted same-directory import (the mock lives *inside* the component's folder), and rewriting all 60 to `@/components/FamilyTree/FamilyTree` is churn that makes them longer without making them clearer.

So there's a judgement call to make before this is worth wiring up:

questions.question: How should the rule treat the 60 `__mocks__/../<Component>` imports?

options.label: Exempt `__mocks__` dirs (Recommended)
options.description: Add a `files: ['**/__mocks__/**']` override turning the rule off there. Rule lands green immediately; only the 4 real violations need fixing. Codifies the mock-imports-its-subject pattern as intentional.

options.label: Convert all 60 to `@/`
options.description: No exemption — one uniform rule with no carve-outs. Costs a 60-file mechanical diff, and each mock import gets longer.

options.label: Add a tsconfig path (Recommended)
options.description: Map something like `@root/*` to `./*`, so the spec imports `@root/mdx-components`. Keeps the ESLint rule free of file-specific carve-outs.

options.label: Move mdx-components into src/
options.description: Relocate the file so `@/mdx-components` just works. Cleanest long-term, but touches next.config.mjs / MDX wiring and risks breaking the build.

options.label: One-line eslint-disable
options.description: Leave the import as-is with an inline disable comment and a note. Smallest change; one permanent exception in the tree.
